args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of about 18%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Mitigation: rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying, and review why a release that failed in staging was promoted.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), and about 18% of requests were failing.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. All three regions are now on v2.3.0. A follow-up check shows the service healthy, with about 0.2% of requests failing.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It says what failed, what I did and how the service looks now. It also lists two follow-ups:
  - Find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.
  - Review how v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also failed in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
